cldr_metadata.why: CLDR's territoryAlias table -- a third register's decision about the same dead codes.

iso3166ma_reserved_2003.why: The ISO 3166/MA's own list of reserved code elements, dated 2003-07-28, mirrored by the Hong Kong government. Carries the reallocation rule and the two reservation tables. The PDF is hashed here; its text could not be extracted locally (no working extractor in this environment) and was read through a server-side extraction service -- see sources/PROVENANCE.md.

iso_3166_1.why: The currently assigned country codes, same compilation, used to ask which dead codes are in use again.

iso_3166_3.why: ISO 3166-3, the register of formerly used country names, as compiled by the iso-codes project. A THIRD-PARTY COMPILATION: ISO's own list is behind a paywall and iso.org returns 403 to this host. Every load-bearing entry is cross-checked against the CLDR aliases, the IANA registry and the ISO 3166/MA's own 2003 reserved-code list.

iso_org_3166_3.why: ISO 3166-3:2013's catalogue entry. Expected to fail from this host.

iso_org_country_codes.why: ISO's own free description of the three parts. Expected to fail from this host.

rfc1766.why: 1995. Names ISO 3166:1988 as its reference edition -- the date that fixes the floor.

rfc3066.why: 2001. The intermediate rule: two-letter subtags are ISO 3166 codes 'or subsequently assigned'.

rfc4645.why: 2006. The founding import rules of the IANA registry, including rule 2's parenthesis about 'CS'.

rfc4646.why: 2006. The first version of the region-subtag rules, for the diff against RFC 5646.

rfc5646.why: 2009. BCP 47 as it stands, including the recycled-code rule in section 2.2.4.

subtag_registry.why: The registry itself. Measured here on its ISO 3166-1 upstream rather than its ISO 639 one.
